title: Open the right kind of space in Claude
summary: Read a rate card once, then keep it handy for a second visit.

intro.what: Claude is a helper you can talk to. For one question, open a chat. A Project keeps related chats and files together for use over time.
intro.features: You can add a file, save project instructions, link a service or search the web. Choose where the facts should come from.
intro.exchange: Keep a sample mail rule in a Project. Ask whether a blank subject matches the rule.
intro.m365: Put a practice agenda and its follow-up in one Project. Find what changed.
intro.developer: Save the rules of a dice game with its code. Check that a new turn uses the right rules.
sources: How Claude Projects use shared reference material
Where Cowork runs and how it reaches local files

sections.title: Start with a small file
paragraphs: Make a text file with two lines: “Weekday rate: $2 an hour. Weekend rate: $3 an hour.” Attach it to a new chat. Ask for the cost of two hours on Saturday. If you want to ask more questions tomorrow, create a Project and add the file there. Put “Show the rule you used” in the project instructions.
sources: How Claude Projects use shared reference material

sections.title: Check the row Claude read
paragraphs: The answer should be $6. Saturday uses the weekend row. Two hours times $3 is $6. Now add “Event day: $8 for the whole visit, including weekends.” Say that this Saturday is an event day and ask again. Open the file yourself. If it still says $6, ask it to read the whole event-day line.
sources: File and image support in Claude

sections.title: Decide what Claude may read
paragraphs: Attach a file to use the exact copy in front of you. A connector links an app you have given Claude permission to read. Search can find public pages. Suppose a new rate card replaces an old one. Ask for the date on both cards. Read the dates and rates yourself before picking the rule to use.
sources: Web search and citations in Claude
File and image support in Claude

title: Pick a Claude model with a fair test
summary: Give two models the same short job. Check the answer and the cost.

intro.what: A model is the part of Claude that reads your request and writes back. The menu in a chat can offer a different list from the API used by an app.
intro.features: Some models give fast answers to simple jobs. Others spend more time on hard ones. The API lists a price for what you send and a price for what comes back.
intro.exchange: Have each model sort three pretend mail warnings. Count the wrong labels.
intro.m365: Try the same two meeting notes with each model. Check who owns each task using role labels.
intro.developer: Ask two models to fix one scoring bug. Try the same three turns with both fixes.
sources: Model, effort and thinking controls in Claude

sections.title: Pick two to try
paragraphs: Make an answer card before you start. It might say “Date missing. Two events. One time overlap.” Give each model the same notes. See which items it catches. These are direct API IDs.

rows: Sort many short notes into groups.
Make one clear edit to a small app.
Trace a mistake through a few files.
Try a hard case that other choices keep missing.

sections.title: Read the two prices
paragraphs: Input is what you send. Output is what the model writes. A token is a piece of text. These base prices are in US dollars per million tokens. Read across a row for one model. Longer requests and extra tools can cost more.

exercise.prompt: Which row changes when a request gets long?
answer: The first row applies through {{model.claude.haiku.threshold}}. Above that its rates are {{model.claude.haiku.long-rate}}. Check the price page when you plan a large job.

sections.title: Make room for your answer
paragraphs: These models have a context window of {{model.claude.context}} and an output limit of {{model.claude.max-out}}. Think of a context window as a desk that must hold both the notes and the answer. Break a thick packet into named parts. Ask for the page behind each answer.

In chat, open the model menu to see the effort choices on your account. Try a higher effort on a question that went wrong. Check whether it now gives the right rule. A related model, {{model.claude.mythos.name}}, has restricted access.
sources: Model, effort and thinking controls in Claude
API model lifecycle and retirement dates

title: Edit a tiny app with Claude Code
summary: Build a date filter and check that the old buttons still work.

intro.what: Claude Code helps with files in a coding project. It can read a file, suggest an edit and run a test.
intro.features: You can use it in a desktop app or a terminal, a window where you type commands. It can show a plan and a list of what changed.
intro.exchange: Add a date filter to a pretend mail report. Keep every row when the filter is clear.
intro.m365: Find which file supplies the due date in a sample task list. Change that file in a practice copy.
intro.developer: Add a date picker to a tiny book index. Make sure old links still open their pages.
sources: How Claude Code reads project instructions
Microsoft Learn · paging Microsoft Graph results

sections.title: Choose the folder first
paragraphs: Open Claude Code on your computer. Choose the practice folder that holds your book or app. Ask “List the files you see. Which file draws the index?” Look for a file name you recognize. A copy in the cloud may be missing edits that you have only saved on your computer.

sections.title: Ask for a plan, then check the edit
paragraphs: Switch to Plan Mode. Ask for a date filter and a way to clear it. Tell Claude to keep old page links working. Read the plan and allow the file edit when it fits. Open the app. Pick a day with an entry, then one with no entries. Clear the date. Check the full list. Open one of your old links.

sections.title: Leave a note for the next session
paragraphs: A text file named CLAUDE.md can tell Claude how to run your tests. Write “Open the index. Pick a date. Clear the date. Check the full list.” Keep it beside the project files. The /model command shows model choices. Try {{model.claude.sonnet.name}} on a small edit. Try {{model.claude.opus.name}} when one fix touches several files. Count the extra fixes each one needs.
sources: How Claude Code reads project instructions
Model selection and usage in Claude Code

title: Use Cowork, Chrome and linked apps
summary: Try reading a page, then let a helper draft a file you can review.

intro.what: Claude in Chrome sits beside a web page. Cowork can work through a job with tools and files. A connector lets Claude use a service you choose.
intro.features: You can ask the browser helper to read a page, give Cowork a practice folder or ask for a draft before anything is sent.
intro.exchange: Give Cowork three pretend mail notices. Ask it which ones describe the same issue.
intro.m365: Use a practice folder with two meeting plans and list any time clashes.
intro.developer: Open your draft help page beside Claude and find the line that tells a player how to win.
sources: Claude in Chrome availability and controls
Where Cowork runs and how it reaches local files

sections.title: Use a browser tab for a reading job
paragraphs: In desktop Chrome, open the Claude side panel beside a public event calendar. Ask “Which events run after six? Give the time and the event link.” Pick one result and click its link yourself. Check that the evening time is for that event. On iPad, you can paste the page text into a chat.
sources: Claude in Chrome availability and controls
Web search and citations in Claude

sections.title: Give Cowork a folder and a finish line
paragraphs: Put two sample notes in a practice folder. One says “Set up at 10.” The other says “Check the door at 10.” Give Cowork that folder. Ask for a fresh file that lists the clash. Open the new file and check that both tasks appear. A cloud task can keep running when you leave. To read a desktop folder, the desktop app needs to stay connected.
sources: Where Cowork runs and how it reaches local files

sections.title: Check the permission screen
paragraphs: A request to read an event list needs access to that list. A request to send a message changes what other people see. Practice by asking for a draft only. Read the words, the recipient and the date. If the tool asks to send it, stop at the review screen. You already have the draft you asked for.
sources: Claude in Chrome availability and controls
Where Cowork runs and how it reaches local files

title: Read a picture and make a drawing with Claude
summary: Try a sign, a score screen and a plan for a short movie.

intro.what: Claude can read an image and describe it. It can write drawing instructions called SVG. A browser draws the lines and shapes from those instructions.
intro.features: An Artifact opens a piece of work beside the chat. Claude Design helps make pages you can edit. Claude can also plan the shots for a video.
intro.exchange: Ask it to read a picture of a made-up mail error. Mark any number you cannot see.
intro.m365: Draw the three steps for joining a practice meeting. Check the order on the picture.
intro.developer: Draw a large Start button for a game. Test its size on the screen you will use.
sources: Claude’s image and interactive visual capabilities
Creating and exporting with Claude Design

sections.title: Read a sign, then draw one
paragraphs: Start with a clear picture of a sign. Ask for its words and hours. Cover the last digit in a time and try again. A good answer should say which digit is hard to read. Now ask for an SVG sign with a simple arrow and no words. Open the drawing. Zoom in to see if the edge stays sharp.
sources: Claude’s image and interactive visual capabilities
File and image support in Claude

sections.title: Try an Artifact
paragraphs: Ask for a score screen with two players, a box for each score and an Add turn button. Open the Artifact beside the chat. Enter 3 and 2. Press the button. Ask for a bigger label if the totals are hard to read. Export a working page if another person needs to use its buttons. A PDF can show what the screen looks like.
sources: Creating and exporting with Claude Design

sections.title: Plan a movie shot
paragraphs: Ask for three shots of a game being set up. Give them lengths of two, three and five seconds. Check that ten seconds is enough for the action. Use a tool that makes video to draw the moving frames. Watch the cut between shots. Does the same token stay on the board? Use the plan to tell the video tool exactly what to fix.
sources: Claude’s image and interactive visual capabilities
